items.label: Parking Brake
items.info: Below the PFD. Prevents the aircraft from rolling during prep.

items.label: BAT 1 / BAT 2
items.info: Overhead Panel. Two independent lithium-ion battery switches. Both ON to bring up the avionics bus and FADEC power.

items.label: GEN 1 / GEN 2
items.info: Overhead Panel. GEN 1 is a generator that feeds the ESS, MAIN and EMER buses. GEN 2 is an alternator that feeds only the ESS and EMER buses. Switch both ON so they come online after engine start.

items.label: Strobe Lights
items.info: Overhead Panel. The anti-collision lights on each wingtip and the tail. The SF50 has no separate beacon. Required before engine start so people on the ramp know the engine is about to spool.

items.label: CAS Messages
items.info: PFD. Crew Alerting System panel on the PFD. Review all advisory and caution messages after power-up; clear any that are expected.

items.label: FMS Preflight
items.info: Garmin Perspective Touch+ touchscreen. Walk through the FPL page: enter departure/destination, load or build the route, set SID and STAR. Then open PERF for cruise altitude and V-speeds. CAPS PIN must still be in at this point.

items.label: Altimeters
items.info: PFD. Set barometric reference to current field QNH on both PFD baro knobs.

items.label: Transponder
items.info: MFD. Enter the assigned squawk code. Leave in STBY until lineup.

items.label: Passengers
items.info: Cabin. Brief occupants on seat belts, emergency exits, and CAPS operation before engine start.

items.label: Seat Belts
items.info: Cabin. Confirm all occupants are belted before start.

items.label: Thrust Lever
items.info: Center Pedestal. Confirm the thrust lever is fully aft in the IDLE detent before starting. Introducing power during start causes a hot start.

items.label: Brakes
items.info: Rudder Pedals. Apply toe brakes to hold the aircraft stationary during start.

items.label: Engine Knob
items.info: Center Pedestal. Two positions: RUN and OFF. Move to RUN to arm the FADEC and turn on the electric fuel pump. The separate ENGINE START/STOP button starts the engine.

items.label: Fuel Pump
items.info: PFD. Verify the FUEL PUMP ON CAS advisory is displayed after the Engine Knob goes to RUN, confirming the electric boost pump is running.

items.label: Engine Start/Stop
items.info: Overhead Panel. Momentary button. Press to engage the starter motor. Monitor N2: expect light-off within 8 seconds. At roughly 25% N2 the FADEC should indicate positive N1. Monitor ITT — abort if no light-off by 8 sec or if ITT exceeds limits.

items.label: Engine Instruments
items.info: MFD. Watch N1, N2, ITT, and oil pressure as the engine spools. Expect positive N1 indication by 25% N2. ITT must stay within the start limit arc. Oil pressure should enter the green band shortly after stabilization.

items.label: EIS
items.info: MFD. Engine Indication System. Once stabilized at idle, all parameters should show green — N1, N2, ITT, oil pressure, fuel flow.

items.label: Oxygen Master
items.info: Overhead Panel. Opens the oxygen supply to the crew masks. Required for flight above 12,500 ft MSL. Set after engine start when normal electrical power is stable.

items.label: Avionics Init
items.info: PFD / MFD. Allow the Garmin Perspective Touch+ suite to complete initialization. Verify both PFD and MFD show valid data, no red X flags.

items.label: BLEED Switch
items.info: Overhead Panel. Two positions: BLEED and FRESH. Don't set BLEED until BAT 1 and BAT 2 have been ON for 2 minutes or more. BLEED routes engine bleed air into the cabin for pressurization.

items.label: ECS Control Panel
items.info: Overhead Panel. Environmental Control System. Set cabin temperature and airflow as desired for occupant comfort.

items.label: CAPS Pin
items.info: Overhead (ceiling) CAPS handle. Remove and stow after engine start. A CAPS PIN CAS advisory clears once removed.

items.label: COM / NAV
items.info: MFD. Set departure ATIS, clearance delivery, and ground frequencies. Tune NAV/GPS for departure.

items.label: ATIS
items.info: COM Radio. Get current weather and NOTAM information before calling for taxi.

items.label: Altimeters
items.info: PFD. Confirm baro setting matches current ATIS. Cross-check both PFD baro knobs.

items.label: Pitch Trim
items.info: Center Pedestal. Set pitch trim for takeoff and check it on the trim indicator on the MFD.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Overhead Panel flap switch or center pedestal. 50% flap (half extension) is the normal takeoff setting for the SF50. VFE at 50% is 190 KIAS.

items.label: Flight Controls
items.info: Sidestick and rudder pedals. Move through full travel and verify correct deflection on the PFD control surface indicators.

items.label: Parking Brake
items.info: Below the PFD. Release before taxi; the click spot is just right of the handle.

items.label: Brakes
items.info: Rudder Pedals. Apply briefly during initial taxi roll to confirm normal stopping power.

items.label: TO/GA Button
items.info: Thrust lever, the thumb button on the side of the handle. Sets the flight director to takeoff pitch. ROL appears on the PFD mode annunciator when it is pressed.

items.label: CAS Messages
items.info: PFD. Verify no unexpected advisory or caution messages before takeoff. A TAKEOFF EMER BAT message before lineup is a no-go item.

items.label: Probe Heat
items.info: Overhead Panel. Heats pitot and static probes to prevent ice blockage. Switch on before entering the runway.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Overhead Panel. Forward-facing landing lights. ON when entering the runway.

items.label: Transponder
items.info: MFD. Switch from STBY to ALT at runway entry. The Vision Jet's traffic system (TCAS I) gives traffic advisories only, with no resolution advisories.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Overhead Panel. Confirm 50% flap setting has not changed since taxi. VFE 50% is 190 KIAS.

items.label: Pitch Trim
items.info: MFD trim indicator. Confirm trim is still set for takeoff.

items.label: CAS Messages
items.info: PFD. The specific check here is confirming no TAKEOFF EMER BAT message is present. Any other caution or advisory should be understood before proceeding.

items.label: Brakes
items.info: Rudder Pedals. Hold brakes while advancing the thrust lever to verify engine instruments are normal before releasing.

items.label: Thrust Lever
items.info: Center Pedestal. Advance to the T/O detent. The FADEC limits thrust automatically — no manual ITT management required. Verify the EIS shows expected N1 and ITT.

items.label: Engine Instruments
items.info: MFD. Confirm N1, ITT, N2, and oil pressure are all green before releasing brakes.

items.label: Brakes
items.info: Rudder Pedals. Release brakes to begin the roll once instruments confirm normal thrust.

items.label: Rotate
items.info: Sidestick. Rotate at 85 KIAS to 10° nose-up, then follow the flight director.

items.label: Gear
items.info: Instrument Panel. Retract at positive rate of climb. VLO retract is 150 KIAS.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Overhead Panel. Retract above 115 KIAS, clear of obstacles.

items.label: Thrust Lever
items.info: Center Pedestal. After reaching a safe altitude, reduce from T/O to MCT (Maximum Continuous Thrust). T/O thrust is time-limited to 5 minutes. MCT is the maximum un-time-limited power setting for climb.

items.label: Engine Parameters
items.info: MFD. Confirm all engine indications remain in the green arc throughout the climb.

items.label: Autopilot
items.info: Glareshield AP button. Engage at own discretion once the aircraft is established in the climb with gear and flaps up.

items.label: Cabin Pressure
items.info: MFD. Verify cabin altitude is climbing at a normal rate and differential pressure is building correctly.

items.label: Ice Protection
items.info: Overhead Panel. Activate ENGINE IPS and WING/STAB IPS if operating in visible moisture at temperatures at or below +5°C.

items.label: Altimeters
items.info: PFD baro knobs. Set both to STD (29.92 in Hg / 1013 hPa) when passing transition altitude.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Overhead Panel. Not required above 10,000 ft.

items.label: EIS
items.info: MFD. Engine Indication System. Periodically confirm N1, N2, ITT, oil pressure and fuel flow are all stable in the green.

items.label: Thrust Lever
items.info: Center Pedestal. Click the spot at the back of the thrust lever handle to snap to MCT, or let the autothrottle manage thrust in FMS mode. Max cruise is 311 KTAS at FL280.

items.label: Ice Protection
items.info: Overhead Panel. Enable ENGINE IPS and WING/STAB IPS if in icing conditions. Max operating altitude is 31,000 ft.

items.label: Approach Briefing
items.info: Cockpit. Review the arrival ATIS, approach type, MDA/DH, missed approach procedure, and destination field elevation before starting descent.

items.label: Landing Field Elevation
items.info: MFD. Confirm the destination airport elevation is loaded correctly in the FMS for pressurization scheduling.

items.label: Minimums
items.info: PFD. Set MDA or DH (decision height) on the PFD for the planned approach.

items.label: Thrust Lever
items.info: Center Pedestal. Pull back as needed to start down and hold the descent speed.

items.label: Altimeters
items.info: PFD baro knobs. Set local QNH when passing transition flight level on descent.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Overhead Panel. On below 10,000 ft.

items.label: Approach Mode
items.info: Autopilot control panel, APR button. Arms the autopilot to capture the final approach course and glidepath once the approach is loaded.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Overhead Panel. Set initial 50% flap for the approach. Maximum speed with flaps at 50% is 190 KIAS. Maintain below 140 KIAS before adding full flap.

items.label: Airspeed
items.info: PFD. Hold 140 KIAS once flaps are at 50%. Flaps 50% are limited to 190 KIAS and gear extension to 210 KIAS.

items.label: Landing Gear
items.info: Instrument Panel. Extend gear below 210 KIAS. Confirm three green gear-down indications on the MFD.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Overhead Panel. Select 100% for normal conditions, 50% maximum if there is ice on the airframe. Maximum speed with flaps at 100% is 150 KIAS.

items.label: Cabin Pressure
items.info: MFD. Verify differential pressure approaching zero on descent to field elevation.

items.label: Autopilot
items.info: Glareshield AP button. Disconnect before final approach. Exact timing is pilot discretion, but off before short final is standard.

items.label: Windshield IPS
items.info: Overhead Panel. Fluid spray reduces visibility, so turn windshield ice protection off before landing.

items.label: Airspeed
items.info: PFD. Target approach speed is VAPP — approximately 97 KIAS (VRef 87 KIAS plus ~10 kt wind correction). Stall speed with flaps is 67 KIAS.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Overhead Panel. Confirm landing lights are illuminated on final approach.

items.label: Thrust Lever
items.info: Center Pedestal. Retard to idle over the threshold for touchdown. The SF50 has no thrust reversers — braking is entirely via wheel brakes.

items.label: Brakes
items.info: Rudder Pedals. Apply brakes after mains touch. The SF50 has no thrust reversers or spoilers, so brake early and consistently. Landing ground roll is approximately 1,628 ft.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Overhead Panel. Retract flaps after clearing the runway.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Overhead Panel. Off after clearing the active runway.

items.label: Probe Heat
items.info: Overhead Panel. No longer required once clear of the runway.

items.label: Wing / Stab IPS
items.info: Overhead Panel. Ice protection systems off after landing.

items.label: Engine IPS
items.info: Overhead Panel. Engine inlet ice protection off after clearing the runway.

items.label: Brakes
items.info: Rudder Pedals. Check brake temperature on MFD if available. Confirm pedal response is normal before reaching the gate.

items.label: Thrust Lever
items.info: Center Pedestal. Allow the engine to run at idle for at least 2 minutes before shutdown.

items.label: Parking Brake
items.info: Below the PFD. Set after the idle cooldown is complete.

items.label: Bleed
items.info: Overhead Panel. Two positions: BLEED and FRESH. Set FRESH before shutting the engine down.

items.label: GEN 1 / GEN 2
items.info: Overhead Panel. Turn off both before the Engine Knob goes to OFF.

items.label: Engine Knob
items.info: Center Pedestal. Two positions: RUN and OFF. Move to OFF to close the FADEC fuel metering valve and stop the electric fuel pump.

items.label: Engine Start/Stop
items.info: Overhead Panel. Press the Engine START/STOP button to complete the shutdown sequence after the Engine Knob is in OFF.

items.label: N2
items.info: MFD. Wait for N2 to drop below 24% before removing aircraft power. Switching the batteries off earlier can log FADEC faults.

items.label: CAPS Pin
items.info: Overhead (ceiling) CAPS handle. Put the safety pin back so the parachute handle can't be pulled on the ground.

items.label: Lights
items.info: Overhead Panel. Turn off all external and interior lights: strobe, landing, navigation and cabin.

items.label: Oxygen Master
items.info: Overhead Panel. Close the oxygen supply valve after all occupants have deplaned.

items.label: BAT 1 / BAT 2
items.info: Overhead Panel. Master battery switches off last. Powers down the avionics bus and all remaining systems.

description: The world's first single-engine personal jet, the Vision Jet makes jet performance accessible to single-pilot operators.
